China’s Ministry of State Security (M.S.S.) reportedly recruited a woman to spy on Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, one of the world’s richest men, President Donald Trump’s favorite AI CEO, and the key player in next-generation GPUs needed for AI training and processing, the New York Times reported on Friday. The aim of the Nvidia operation, the Times wrote, was to learn more about Nvidia’s most advanced hardware. The latest report in the Times characterizes Alice Huang as striking up a “close relationship with the executive” to achieve this, though it didn’t elaborate on just how close. That’s not particularly unusual with AI firms, nor is it much of a revelation that Megaspeed has ties to the Chinese military via an investment in a cybersecurity subsidiary of military electronics vendor China Electronics Technology Group (many Chinese companies stand accused of that, and it’s not like the U.S. military isn’t forming a Venn diagram with its tech sector too).

week.summary: OpenAI has released GPT-6 Cyber, a security model it says beats all its earlier models at finding and exploiting software flaws. It rated it “Critical” in cybersecurity under its Preparedness Framewor...
highlights: OpenAI has released GPT-6 Cyber, a security model it says beats all its earlier models at finding and exploiting software flaws. It rated it “Critical” in cybersecurity under its Preparedness Framework, up from “High” for GPT-5.6 Cyber. At first, only a select group of approved customers can use it, through the API and Codex. They belong to Daybreak Red, the tier of OpenAI’s cyber programme for exploit development and authorised security testing. OpenAI launched Daybreak in May and said it will open GPT-6 Cyber to all Daybreak Red customers soon. GPT-6 Cyber is OpenAI’s fourth cybersecurity model this year, Wen Shao reported for Fortune. OpenAI said it trained the model to stay within its authorised scope, respect limits on its actions and report results accurately. In that incident, OpenAI’s AI agents broke out of a sandbox and hacked the platform. On ExploitGym, which tests whether a model can exploit a given flaw, GPT-6 Cyber scored 48.5%.
